## Solution

**Key observation.** Consider the derivative of $e^{nx}\tan^n x$:

$$\frac{d}{dx}\!\left[e^{nx}\tan^n x\right] = n\,e^{nx}\tan^n x + e^{nx}\cdot n\tan^{n-1}x\,\sec^2 x = n\,e^{nx}\tan^{n-1}x\!\left(\tan x + 1 + \tan^2 x\right).$$

Since $\tan x + \sec^2 x = \tan x + 1 + \tan^2 x$, this gives

$$\frac{d}{dx}\!\left[e^{nx}\tan^n x\right] = n\,e^{nx}\!\left(\tan^{n-1}x + \tan^n x + \tan^{n+1}x\right).$$

**Evaluating the integral.** Therefore

$$I_n := \int_0^{\pi/4} e^{nx}\!\left(\tan^{n-1}x+\tan^n x+\tan^{n+1}x\right)dx = \frac{1}{n}\Big[e^{nx}\tan^n x\Big]_{0}^{\pi/4}.$$

At $x=\pi/4$: $e^{n\pi/4}\cdot\tan^n(\pi/4)=e^{n\pi/4}\cdot 1=e^{n\pi/4}$. At $x=0$: $e^{0}\cdot 0^n=0$. Hence

$$I_n = \frac{e^{n\pi/4}}{n}.$$

**Computing the limit.** Now

$$\sqrt[n]{I_n} = \left(\frac{e^{n\pi/4}}{n}\right)^{1/n} = e^{\pi/4}\cdot n^{-1/n}.$$

Since $n^{1/n}\to 1$ as $n\to\infty$, we have $\sqrt[n]{I_n}\to e^{\pi/4}$, a finite constant. Thus

$$\sqrt[n]{I_n}-1 \;\longrightarrow\; e^{\pi/4}-1 \quad\text{(a finite constant)},$$

and dividing by $n\to\infty$:

$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\!\left(\sqrt[n]{I_n}-1\right) = \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{e^{\pi/4}\,n^{-1/n}-1}{n} = 0.$$

**Conclusion.** The limit equals $\boxed{0}$.
